- scripts/claude_pool_daily_usage.sh:daily_usage_send retry_hours validation (and daily_usage_start_hour by symmetry), lines ~167 and ~71 | HARDENING_SUGGESTION (not a finding; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1)
  PROBLEM: The regex `^0*[0-9]{1,2}$` limits the value to 1-2 significant digits but does not limit the total string length, so a value with 30+ leading zeros still matches.
  WHY: The reviewer says bash arithmetic `$((10#...))` "could overflow on a 64-bit bash without `--enable-arb-int`, potentially wrapping to a negative number that passes both `-gt 23` and the `[ retry_hours -gt 0 ]` deferral guard". Suggested fix: `[[ ${#retry_hours} -le 6 ]] && [[ "${retry_hours}" =~ ^0*[0-9]{1,2}$ ]] && [ "$((10#${retry_hours}))" -le 23 ]`, about 2 lines per function. The reviewer rates it "minor improvement; depends on bash compile flags and env var from trusted workflow var; not a real production trigger". No issues were reported in any review category.
